## You need:

Gladys Assistent > Version 5.2

External Integration Transitous Depatures

Internet Access for Your Gladys Assistant Installation

## You get:

You'll receive an external integration for Galdys Assistant. 
This integration automatically displays the next 6 public transportation departures in a clear, easy-to-read widget—from buses to trains, ferries, and cable cars.
All of this within a configurable radius around your home.

Example:

![Lissabon – Beispielansicht der Transitous-Integration](https://github.com/tomgermany/gladys-transitous-departures/raw/HEAD/./test/lissabon.png)

Result: For each of the six tiles, the nearest stop is first determined once. That is, the nearest bus stop, nearest ferry, and nearest rail stop.
The next departure from that stop is then displayed.
This means: If there is only one stop within your search radius, you will see the next six departures.
If multiple stops are found, they are displayed using color coding.

## Configuration

1. Install the external integration either through Gladys Assistant (recommended)
 or in Gladys Assistant with direct access to GitHub.

2. After Installation check that Integration is running.
   
3. Open your Dashboard and go into Edit Modus and there add the new Widget.
   Select this Integration Widget.
   
4. When adding the widget to your dashboard, you’ll need some information:
   
a.) Your geolocation as the starting point
 (or choose location from Gladys Assistant)
 
b.) The diameter of the search radius.

c.) The refresh interval in 10-minute increments.

d.) A unique identifier for API access at https://transitous.org/.
This identifier must be unique—for example, an email address or website.
It is stored by the integration only in the configuration field there.
The integration neither retrieves nor documents this identifier.
Everything remains with you. Transitous.org uses this identifier to manage the load on its IT infrastructure.
Keep in mind the data provider when setting this. We recommend 15 minutes.

8. After filling out this information, save it and place the widget where you want it.


## Troubleshooting

The integration logs everything it does: check the integration logs from the
Gladys UI (or `docker logs` on the host) with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` for the full
detail.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Transitous Departures asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Widget setup information | `section` | No | Before adding the widget to your dashboard, determine the coordinates of your chosen location. You need latitude and longitude in decimal format, for example 49.350 and 8.690. When adding the widget, you can then configure the search radius, number of departures and refresh interval. The default search radius is 2,000 metres. Timetable data: Transitous. Information about data sources and attribution: https:\/\/transitous.org/sources/ |

## How to install Transitous Departures in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Transitous Departures appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/tomgermany/gladys-transitous-departures:3.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/tomgermany/gladys-transitous-departures](https://github.com/tomgermany/gladys-transitous-departures).

Transitous Departures requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Transitous Departures is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [tomgermany](https://github.com/tomgermany), not by the Gladys core team.
